M. John Harrison has won the 2026 Booker Prize with ‘The End of Everything’

WORDS Kirsty Thatcher    PUBLISHED Tue, 10 Nov 2026 - 9:03 am

Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 2:20
Instaread

M John Harrison has been named the winner of the 2026 Booker Prize for his novel The End of Everything, one of the most prestigious awards in contemporary literature.

The winning title was selected from a shortlist of six novels, narrowed down from 163 submissions by this year's judging panel. Chaired by British classicist and author Dame Mary Beard, the panel also included musician Jarvis Cocker, American novelist Patricia Lockwood, poet Raymond Antrobus and Guardian critic Rebecca Liu.

 

What is the book about?

As the title suggests, The End of Everything is a post-apocalyptic novel. It follows Phillip Tennent, who makes his living collecting artefacts washed up along the English Channel. But when Phillip discovers a strange creature in the water, he finds himself tasked with transporting it inland – in turn kickstarting a life-altering journey.

 

Who is M. John Harrison?

This is the British writer's 13th novel, and first time on the Booker Prize shortlist. At 81-years-old, he is the oldest-ever Booker Prize winner.

Harrison's other notable works include The Centauri Device, Climbers, The Course of the Heart and The Sunken Land Begins to Rise Again.

While the Booker might be the most prestigious award he has received, his previous accolades include the Boardman Tasker Prize for Climbers, the Arthur C. Clarke Award for Nova Swing and the Goldsmiths Prize for The Sunken Land Begins to Rise Again.

 

Who was shortlisted for the 2026 Booker Prize?

The 2026 shortlist featured five other novels, including:

  • The Disappearers by Marlon James
  • Black Bag by Luke Kennard
  • May We Feed the King by Rebecca Perry
  • The Things We Never Say by Elizabeth Strout
  • John of John by Douglas Stuart

 

What is the Booker Prize?

First awarded in 1969, the Booker Prize recognises the best work of long-form fiction published in the UK or Ireland during the eligible year. Open to novels written in English by authors of any nationality, it is widely regarded as one of the most significant awards in contemporary literature.

The winning author receives £50,000, while each of the other shortlisted writers takes home £2,500.

A important distinction to make is that the Booker Prize is separate to the International Booker Prize, which recognises fiction originally written in another language and translated into English.

The Sydney Mardi Gras 2027 program is in full bloom

WORDS Samantha Corry     PHOTOGRAPHY courtesy Sydney Gay and Lesbian Mardi Gras website    PUBLISHED Thu, 5 Nov 2026 - 3:45 pm

It's the most wonderful time of the year – and we're not just talking about the upcoming festive season. The official program for the 2027 Sydney Gay and Lesbian Mardi Gras has just dropped and we're already planning what to wear and which events to add to our calendars.

Running from 12 February until 7 March 2027, next year's festival is themed 'Hyperbloom'. "HYPERBLOOM is a celebration of everything that makes our communities extraordinary," says Sydney Gay and Lesbian Mardi Gras CEO Jesse Matheson. "It’s about coming together and taking up space to flourish."

Festival goers can look forward to three weeks packed with colour, spectacle, and imagination. Read on for everything you need to know about next year's program.

 

When is Mardi Gras 2027?

The 2027 festival will run in Sydney from Friday 12 February to Sunday 7 March 2027. Almost a month of celebrations and pride.

 

When is the parade?

The question on everyones lips. Next year the Sydney Mardi Gras parade will be towards the end of the program on Saturday 6 March 2027.

We can expect another big year of marchers, floats and performers all making their way across Oxford Street, Flinders Street and Anzac Parade. And if you want a higher viewing point, no stress, there will be accessible look outs along Flinders Street, with Glitter Club at Taylor Square too.

 

What else is on the program?

Kicking off the festivities is Fair Day at Victoria Park on Sunday 14 February 2027, also Valentine Day, to bring together communities, retail, food stalls, and entertainment. The line-up includes Rogue Traders, Zipporah, Becca Hatch, Jett Blyton, Dizzy Days and more. It's one of the most anticipated nights on the program.

Of course, the inimitable Diana Ross is also headed to Sydney for a one-night-only performance taking place on the eve of the Sydney Gay and Lesbian Mardi Gras Parade on Friday 5 March 2027, too.

Across Sydney we can expect plenty of performances, exhibitions, panels and pop-ups, curated by Sydney's LGBTQIA+ community. You can find the full program, via the Mardi Gras website.

 

How can I get tickets to the events?

Tickets for presale members go on sale Monday 9 November at 11am AEDT, and general sale is at 12 Thursday November 2026 at 11am AEDT.

You can purchase tickets to all the anticipated events on the program via the Mardi Gras website.
